newsitem.title: USA: Ciena Corp shares surge after opening.
newsitem.headline: Ciena Corp shares surge after opening.

text.p: Ciena Corp shares surged forty percent when they opened for trading on the Nasdaq on Friday after the initial public offering of the maker of telecommunications components.
The shares opened up 10 to 33 from their IPO price of 23 and then settled back slightly, up 9 to 32.

IPO analysts have forecast strong demand for the initial public offering by institutional investors clamoring for an opportunity at the industry. Vince Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald, also cited the company's contracts with Sprint Corp and WorldCom Inc

Ciena makes a "MultiWave 1600" system, which uses dense wavelength division multiplexing ("DWDM") systems to solve traffic congestion problems on high-capacity fiber optic networks. Multiplexing allows the system to manage the different streams of data in the existing fiberoptic network.
The MultiWave system can boost the capacity of a single optical fiber 16-fold, according to the company's prospectus.
Ciena has a three-year non-exclusive supply agreement with Sprint which expires in December 1998 and a supply agreement with WorldCom exclusive through December 1997.

Those two main customers account for substantially all of the Savage, Maryland company's revenues. All of its revenues for the fiscal year ended October 31, 1996 were from Sprint and the company expects all its forecast fiscal 1997 fiscal revenues to be from Sprint and WorldCom, it said in the prospectus.
Ciena offered five million shares for $23 each, with four million offered in the United States and one million offered internationally for a total of five million shares.
The stock was the highest percent gainer on the Nasdaq and one of the most active shares on the Nasdaq.
